# `silk/io/buffered_output`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

A fixed-size output buffer that collects small writes and sends them as larger writes.

## When to use
Use [`BufferedOutput`](#BufferedOutput) when a program makes many small writes to a byte transport and each
transport write has a cost, such as a system call. Make the buffer with [`BufferedOutput.make`](#BufferedOutput.impl.make),
write with [`BufferedOutput.writeAll`](#BufferedOutput.impl.writeAll), and end with [`BufferedOutput.finish`](#BufferedOutput.impl.finish).
To give code that requires `&mut Writer` a buffered destination, wrap that destination, such as
`silk.io.writer_native.StdoutWriter`, in a [`BufferedWriter`](#BufferedWriter).

Each operation has two forms. The deadline form, such as `writeAll`, uses a
`silk.io.byte_duplex.ByteDuplex` transport and a deadline. The `Writer` form, such as
`writeAllWriter`, uses a `silk.io.writer.Writer` provider and has no deadline.

## Details
When a write returns, the buffer owns the accepted bytes. The buffer sends pending bytes to the
transport only when it is full or when the caller flushes it. Input that is longer than the
buffer is not copied: once the pending bytes are sent, it goes to the transport directly. A
flush sends all pending bytes in order, one time each.

A failed transport write or flush makes the buffer terminal. After that, each write and flush
fails with `BufferError.Terminal`. The error reports exactly how many bytes the transport
accepted before the failure.

## Gotchas
Dropping a `BufferedOutput` does not flush it. Pending bytes that are not flushed are lost. Call
[`BufferedOutput.finish`](#BufferedOutput.impl.finish) before the buffer goes out of scope.

## Examples
### Collect two writes into one transport write
```silk
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.io.buffered_input { BufferError }
import silk.io.buffered_output { BufferedOutput }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.io.writer { Writer, WriterError }

// A Writer provider that counts the calls and bytes it receives.
struct CountingWriter {
  calls: usize,
  bytes: usize,
}

impl Writer for CountingWriter {
  effect fn writeAll(self: &mut Self, val: &[u8]) -> ()
    ! WriterError
    ? &mut Writer {
    self.calls = self.calls + 1
    self.bytes = self.bytes + val.length
    return ()
  }

  effect fn flush(self: &mut Self) -> ()
    ! WriterError
    ? &mut Writer {
    return ()
  }
}

pub effect fn main() -> i32
  ! BufferError | OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let mut output = run BufferedOutput.make(64) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  let mut sink = CountingWriter { calls: 0, bytes: 0 }
  run BufferedOutput.writeAllWriter(&mut output, b"hello, ") |> Effect.provideMut<Writer>(&mut sink)
  run BufferedOutput.writeAllWriter(&mut output, b"world") |> Effect.provideMut<Writer>(&mut sink)

  // Both writes fit in the buffer, so the sink has received nothing yet.
  if sink.calls != 0 {
    return 1
  }
  run BufferedOutput.flushWriter(&mut output) |> Effect.provideMut<Writer>(&mut sink)
  if sink.calls != 1 || sink.bytes != 12 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

## `BufferedOutput`

```silk
pub struct BufferedOutput
```

A fixed-size buffer that holds output bytes until the transport receives them.

### When to use

Use it when a program makes many small writes to a byte transport and each transport write has
a cost, such as a system call. Make the buffer with [`BufferedOutput.make`](#BufferedOutput.impl.make), write with
[`BufferedOutput.writeAll`](#BufferedOutput.impl.writeAll), and end with [`BufferedOutput.finish`](#BufferedOutput.impl.finish).

Each operation has two forms. The deadline form, such as `writeAll`, uses a
`silk.io.byte_duplex.ByteDuplex` transport and a deadline. The `Writer` form, such as
`writeAllWriter`, uses a `silk.io.writer.Writer` provider and has no deadline.

### Details

The buffer sends pending bytes to the transport only when it is full or when the caller flushes
it. Input that is longer than the buffer is not copied: once the pending bytes are sent, it goes
to the transport directly. A failed transport write or flush makes the buffer terminal. After
that, each write and flush fails with `BufferError.Terminal`.

The buffer has one allocation of [`BufferedOutput.capacity`](#BufferedOutput.impl.capacity) bytes. The size does not change
after [`BufferedOutput.make`](#BufferedOutput.impl.make). [`BufferedOutput.pending`](#BufferedOutput.impl.pending) gives the number of bytes that the
buffer holds and the transport has not yet received.

### Gotchas

Dropping the buffer does not flush it. Pending bytes that are not flushed are lost. Call
[`BufferedOutput.finish`](#BufferedOutput.impl.finish) before the buffer goes out of scope.

### Associated function `make`

```silk
pub effect fn make(capacity: usize) -> BufferedOutput
  ! BufferError | OutOfMemoryError
  ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns an empty buffer that holds at most `capacity` bytes.

#### Details

This function makes one allocation of `capacity` bytes from the active `Allocator`. The buffer
does no transport operation until the first write that does not fit or the first flush.

#### Errors

- `BufferError.InvalidCapacity` if `capacity` is zero or more than
  `silk.io.buffered_input.MAX_CAPACITY` (1 MiB). The function does not allocate.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the active `Allocator` cannot supply `capacity` bytes.

### Method `isTerminal`

```silk
pub fn isTerminal(self: &Self) -> bool
```

Returns `true` if an earlier transport failure made the buffer unusable.

#### Details

A failed transport write or flush makes the buffer terminal. A terminal buffer stays terminal.
Each later write of one or more bytes and each later flush fails with `BufferError.Terminal`.

<a id="BufferedOutput.impl.writeSome"></a>

### Method `writeSome`

```silk
pub effect fn writeSome(
    self: &mut Self,
    input: &[u8],
    deadline: Option<Instant>,
  ) -> usize
  ! BufferError
  ? &mut ByteDuplex | &mut MonotonicClock
```

Copies the longest prefix of `input` that fits into the buffer and returns its length.

#### When to use

Use `writeSome` when the caller can continue with a partial write, such as a loop that also
does other work. Use [`BufferedOutput.writeAll`](#BufferedOutput.impl.writeAll) to write all of `input`.

#### Details

If the buffer is full, this function first sends all pending bytes to the active `ByteDuplex`
transport. Then it copies input bytes into the free space. If `input` is longer than
[`BufferedOutput.capacity`](#BufferedOutput.impl.capacity), it does not copy: it gives the pending bytes and `input` to
`ByteDuplex.writeSomeVectored`, or only `input` to `ByteDuplex.writeSome` when nothing is
pending, until the transport accepts some input bytes, and returns their count. For a
non-empty `input`, the result is at least 1. For an empty `input`, the result is 0 and the
transport is not used.

#### Errors

- `BufferError.Terminal` if an earlier failure made the buffer terminal.
- `BufferError.WriteFailed` if the transport fails or `deadline` passes. The buffer becomes
  terminal. `drained` gives the number of pending bytes that the transport received.

<a id="BufferedOutput.impl.writeAll"></a>

### Method `writeAll`

```silk
pub effect fn writeAll(
    self: &mut Self,
    input: &[u8],
    deadline: Option<Instant>,
  ) -> ()
  ! BufferError
  ? &mut ByteDuplex | &mut MonotonicClock
```

Copies all of `input` into the buffer and sends pending bytes to the transport when the buffer
is full.

#### When to use

Use `writeAll` for normal output through a `ByteDuplex` transport. Use
[`BufferedOutput.writeAllWriter`](#BufferedOutput.impl.writeAllWriter) for a `Writer` provider.

#### Details

When this function returns, the buffer owns all of `input`, or the transport already has
them. The transport does not necessarily have the buffered bytes yet. Call
[`BufferedOutput.flush`](#BufferedOutput.impl.flush) to send them. A part of `input` that is longer than the buffer goes
to the transport directly, without a copy. `deadline` applies to each transport write that
this call makes.

#### Errors

- `BufferError.Terminal` if an earlier failure made the buffer terminal.
- `BufferError.WriteFailed` if the transport fails or `deadline` passes. The buffer becomes
  terminal. `accepted` gives the number of `input` bytes that the buffer accepted before the
  failure. `drained` gives the number of pending bytes that the transport received.

<a id="BufferedOutput.impl.writeVecAll"></a>

### Method `writeVecAll`

```silk
pub effect fn writeVecAll(
    self: &mut Self,
    inputs: &[Bytes],
    deadline: Option<Instant>,
  ) -> ()
  ! BufferError
  ? &mut ByteDuplex | &mut MonotonicClock
```

Copies each element of `inputs` into the buffer in order, as one [`BufferedOutput.writeAll`](#BufferedOutput.impl.writeAll)
call for each element.

#### When to use

Use `writeVecAll` to write a message that is in more than one `Bytes` value, such as a header
and a body, without first joining the values.

#### Details

Before it writes, this function adds the lengths of all elements and checks the sum for
overflow. `deadline` applies to each transport write that this call makes.

#### Errors

- `BufferError.LengthOverflow` if the sum of the element lengths overflows `usize`. The
  function writes nothing.
- `BufferError.Terminal` if an earlier failure made the buffer terminal.
- `BufferError.WriteFailed` if the transport fails or `deadline` passes. The buffer becomes
  terminal. `accepted` counts the accepted bytes of all elements together, not only the bytes
  of the element that failed.

<a id="BufferedOutput.impl.flush"></a>

### Method `flush`

```silk
pub effect fn flush(
    self: &mut Self,
    deadline: Option<Instant>,
  ) -> ()
  ! BufferError
  ? &mut ByteDuplex | &mut MonotonicClock
```

Sends all pending bytes to the transport and then flushes the transport.

#### When to use

Use `flush` at a message boundary when the other side must receive the bytes now, such as
before the program waits for a response.

#### Details

This function sends pending bytes in order, one time each, and then calls
`ByteDuplex.flush`. When it returns, [`BufferedOutput.pending`](#BufferedOutput.impl.pending) is 0. `deadline` applies to
each transport operation that this call makes.

#### Errors

- `BufferError.Terminal` if an earlier failure made the buffer terminal.
- `BufferError.WriteFailed` if a transport write or the transport flush fails, or if
  `deadline` passes. The buffer becomes terminal. `drained` gives the number of pending bytes
  that the transport received.


Sends all pending bytes to the transport and then flushes the transport.

#### When to use

Use `finish` as the last operation on a buffer. The name shows that the output is complete.
Dropping a buffer does not flush it. [`BufferedOutput.flush`](#BufferedOutput.impl.flush) has the same behavior.

#### Details

This function sends pending bytes in order, one time each, and then calls
`ByteDuplex.flush`. When it returns, [`BufferedOutput.pending`](#BufferedOutput.impl.pending) is 0. `deadline` applies to
each transport operation that this call makes.

#### Errors

- `BufferError.Terminal` if an earlier failure made the buffer terminal.
- `BufferError.WriteFailed` if a transport write or the transport flush fails, or if
  `deadline` passes. The buffer becomes terminal. `drained` gives the number of pending bytes
  that the transport received.

<a id="BufferedOutput.impl.writeSomeWriter"></a>

### Method `writeSomeWriter`

```silk
pub effect fn writeSomeWriter(self: &mut Self, input: &[u8]) -> usize
  ! BufferError
  ? &mut Writer
```

Accepts `input` into the buffer, or sends it to the active `Writer` together with the
pending bytes, and returns the number of accepted bytes. This function has no deadline.

#### When to use

Use `writeSomeWriter` when the destination is a `Writer`, such as standard output, and the
caller can continue with a partial write. Use [`BufferedOutput.writeAllWriter`](#BufferedOutput.impl.writeAllWriter) to write all
of `input`.

#### Details

If `input` fits in the free part of the buffer, this function copies it. If it is shorter
than the whole buffer, this function sends the pending bytes in one `Writer.writeAll`
call and then copies `input`. Otherwise it does not copy: it sends the pending bytes and then
`input` in one `Writer.writeVectored` call, and the buffer is empty after it. If no bytes are
pending, it sends `input` in one `Writer.writeAll` call. Thus the result is the length of
`input` in every case. A provider such as `silk.io.writer_native.StdoutWriter` sends a vectored write
in one system call.

#### Errors

- `BufferError.Terminal` if an earlier failure made the buffer terminal.
- `BufferError.UnknownExternalTransfer` if the `Writer` fails. The buffer becomes terminal.
  The destination can have received some of the pending bytes and of `input`.

<a id="BufferedOutput.impl.writeAllWriter"></a>

### Method `writeAllWriter`

```silk
pub effect fn writeAllWriter(self: &mut Self, input: &[u8]) -> ()
  ! BufferError
  ? &mut Writer
```

Accepts all of `input`. This function uses the active `Writer` provider when `input` does not
fit in the buffer.

#### When to use

Use `writeAllWriter` to buffer many small writes to a `Writer`, such as standard output. Use
[`BufferedOutput.writeAll`](#BufferedOutput.impl.writeAll) for a `ByteDuplex` transport with a deadline.

#### Details

When this function returns, the buffer owns all of `input`, or the `Writer` already has
them. The `Writer` does not necessarily have the buffered bytes yet. Call
[`BufferedOutput.flushWriter`](#BufferedOutput.impl.flushWriter) to send them. An `input` as long as the buffer or longer goes to
the `Writer` without a copy, after the pending bytes, in one
`Writer.writeVectored` call.

#### Errors

- `BufferError.Terminal` if an earlier failure made the buffer terminal.
- `BufferError.UnknownExternalTransfer` if the `Writer` fails. The buffer becomes terminal.
  `progress` gives the number of `input` bytes that the buffer accepted before the failure.
  The destination can have received some of the pending bytes and of `input`.

<a id="BufferedOutput.impl.flushWriter"></a>

### Method `flushWriter`

```silk
pub effect fn flushWriter(self: &mut Self) -> () ! BufferError ? &mut Writer
```

Sends all pending bytes to the active `Writer` in one call and then calls `Writer.flush`.

#### When to use

Use `flushWriter` as the last operation on a buffer that writes to a `Writer`, and at each
point where the destination must have the bytes now.

#### Details

When this function returns, [`BufferedOutput.pending`](#BufferedOutput.impl.pending) is 0.

#### Errors

- `BufferError.Terminal` if an earlier failure made the buffer terminal.
- `BufferError.UnknownExternalTransfer` if `Writer.writeAll` or `Writer.flush` fails. The
  buffer becomes terminal. A `Writer` does not report partial progress. Thus the destination
  can have received some, all, or none of the pending bytes.

<a id="BufferedWriter"></a>

## `BufferedWriter`

```silk
pub struct BufferedWriter<W>
```

A `Writer` that owns a destination `Writer` and collects small writes into larger ones.

### When to use

Use `BufferedWriter` when code that requires `&mut Writer` makes many small writes, such as
field-by-field output, and each write to the destination has a cost, such as a system call.
Wrap the destination, such as `silk.io.writer_native.StdoutWriter`, with [`BufferedWriter.make`](#BufferedWriter.impl.make) and
provide the result as the `Writer`. Use [`BufferedOutput`](#BufferedOutput) when the caller keeps the
destination itself or writes to a `ByteDuplex`.

### Details

`Writer.writeAll` copies small writes into the buffer and sends them when it is full, so the
destination gets one write per fill. A write as long as the buffer or longer goes to the destination
after the pending bytes, without a copy.
`Writer.flush` sends the pending bytes and then flushes the destination. A failed write or
flush of the destination makes the buffer terminal, as for [`BufferedOutput`](#BufferedOutput). Each later
write or flush fails with a [`WriterError`](./io-writer.md#WriterError).

### Gotchas

Dropping a `BufferedWriter` does not flush it. Pending bytes that are not flushed are lost.
Call `Writer.flush` or [`BufferedWriter.finish`](#BufferedWriter.impl.finish) before the writer goes out of scope.

### Examples

```silk
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.io.buffered_input { BufferError }
import silk.io.buffered_output { BufferedWriter }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.io.writer_native { StdoutWriter }
import silk.io.writer { Writer, WriterError }

pub effect fn main() -> i32
  ! BufferError | OutOfMemoryError | WriterError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let mut output = run BufferedWriter<StdoutWriter>.make(StdoutWriter.make(), 4096)
    |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  run Writer.writeString("one ") |> Effect.provideMut<Writer>(&mut output)
  run Writer.writeString("write\n") |> Effect.provideMut<Writer>(&mut output)
  let stdout = run BufferedWriter<StdoutWriter>.finish(move output)
  drop stdout
  return 0
}
```
